root_cause: Observed: four GitHub Actions runs (2026-10-07) report queued, unchanged timestamps and zero jobs, while cancel/force-cancel yield 409 and DELETE yields 403. GitHub provider-internal root cause is unverified. Separate agent-level cause of recurring load is the existing five-minute Recovery Supervisor and hourly Janitor blindly reattempting unrecoverable provider operations without a durable per-run attempt marker.
failed_approaches: Assuming a decreased queued count means record deleted
Repeating same API calls on each five-minute recovery sweep
fix: Keep the existing hourly Repository Janitor as sole bounded provider-ghost owner, detect queued+zero-jobs+24h unchanged provider state and non-authoritative SHA, recheck exact run and jobs before mutations, attempt cancel/force/delete once in a bounded process, persist per-run outcome to existing incident #4655 with markers. Existing five-minute supervisor and generic janitor skip repetitive provider-ghost retries. Poll attempted run IDs for 404/terminal readback and record resolution.
prevention_rule: All present/future chats and agents must search existing incident fingerprint, use exactly the existing Repository Janitor owner, no duplicate schedulers/issues, no repeated 409/403 attempts, no deletion of current main SHA/current PR head/in-progress/real-job runs, no forged green CI. Provider authorization barrier is a real provider handoff, not permission to bypass security.

invariants: do not cancel current main/PR head or a run containing real jobs
do not label a provider 403 failure as resolved
one bounded repair attempt per exact run persisted in canonical incident
GitHub provider support is used only when server-side deletion remains refused
do not bypass required CI, CodeQL or branch protection
historical/shadow/canary replay executes real deterministic provider-ghost guard tests; no weakening of security-sensitive evaluation

terminal_rule: CANDIDATE until protected merge, live scheduled Janitor readback and per-run GitHub API confirmation. Provider incident #4655 remains open until the four exact historic records are terminal or missing, and current gates remain intact.
